lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Make the code link’s destination identifiable without guessing.
items.because: A recruiter should be able to tell whether it leads to a GitHub profile, portfolio, or relevant projects.

items.says: Move the Lumen Travel internship above the university role.
items.because: The internship is more recent, and experience is generally listed in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Add scope or technical context to the website and component-library work.
items.because: “Owned” does not show what was maintained, how widely it was used, or what the contribution involved.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period, comparison, and preview mode’s contribution to the result.
items.because: Readers need to understand what “30 to 6 a month” measures and how the preview mode contributed.

items.says: Clarify what the audit failures refer to and what the checklist covered.
items.because: Readers need context to judge the scale of the before-and-after result.

items.says: Define what “search time” measures.
items.because: User time to find a course and system response time mean different things.

items.says: Mention relevant implementation details if they demonstrate skills needed for target roles.
Specify what the 35% performance measure represents and how it was measured.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it refers to load time, bundle size, or another metric.

items.says: Identify the audit’s scope if space permits.
items.because: That would make the result easier to assess.

items.says: Clarify what the component tests covered or how the regressions were identified.
Verify that lazy-loading the hero image caused the LCP improvement.
items.because: Lazy-loading an above-the-fold hero image can delay it and typically works against improving LCP.

items.says: Storing input in React state does not prevent XSS when rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
items.because: That approach can still expose the application to cross-site scripting.

items.says: Clarify how weekly ridership was measured if the figure is an estimate.
Make sure the two load times were measured under comparable conditions.
items.because: Connection quality and test setup can affect the result.

items.says: Make the project link lead directly to the app or repository.
The listed Vue stack conflicts with the React and TypeScript implementation in the first bullet.
items.because: The project’s technologies should be consistent throughout.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution to the calendar work.
items.because: The team-of-four context makes it important to distinguish your work.

items.says: Clarify how you verified the calendar behavior, including what the tests covered.
The travel-search bullet looks duplicated or misplaced in the library-booking project.
items.because: It appears unrelated to the hackathon and closely resembles the Lumen Travel work above.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: Misspelled skill keywords can be missed by recruiters and ATS.

items.says: Separate languages, frameworks, and tools rather than grouping them all under “Tools.”
items.because: The heading groups technologies from different categories.

items.says: Make the “Methods” category more consistent.
items.because: It mixes practices and architectural concepts.
